SCRATE.evidence: Code-derived. THE STEEL GOODIE CRATE, drawn on a CELL rather than by an object, which is why no heap walk ever reached it. The cartridge keeps one cell-decoration draw table at RAM 0x8020FF58, 39 records of {mode, descriptor} indexed by bits 15..20 of the cell object's word at +8; record 34's descriptor at RAM 0x8020FF48 is the two s32 {88, -1}, meaning body model id 88 and NO SHADOW SET. Model slot = type id + 10, the same bias the walls and terrain use, so 88 is model-table slot 98 (record ROM 0x9ABB8), scene-graph node RAM 0x801B775C, one display list 0x011D4C8 of 8 vertices and 10 triangles. Ten and not twelve because the unseen bottom face is left off; the top face is present. WHAT SELECTS RECORD 34: the 30 OverlayTypeClass registrations (ctor RAM 0x801F2F20, calls ROM 0x1950A8..0x195A18) pass the overlay enum as a1, the IniName pointer as a2 and the draw index as a3. Read directly off the call whose jal is at ROM 0x195A18: a1 = 0x1D = 29, a2 = RAM 0x801C8630 = "SCRATE", a3 = 0x22 = 34. 29 is OVERLAY_STEEL_CRATE counted from the engine's own enum in tiberiandawn/defines.h, so the enum, the name and the draw index agree three ways. THE PIECE OFFSET IS ZERO, measured rather than assumed, and it matters here more than anywhere else: the mode-2 arm at RAM 0x801F57B4 takes a piece index from bits 9..14 of the same cell word (srl 9 / andi 0x3F), indexes the 16-record 12-byte table at RAM 0x802100D0, and ADDS that record's first word to the body id at RAM 0x801F5848 (addu $a0, $a1, $v1) before the draw call at RAM 0x801F5450. Record 0's offset is 0, and the engine writes OverlayData = 0 on every crate it places (tiberiandawn/map.cpp, Place_Random_Crate), so a steel crate always resolves to exactly 88. It has to: slots 99..105 are seven further model-table records ALL holding the wooden crate's node, so any non-zero offset on a steel crate would draw wood. MEASURED EXTENT 185 x 185 x 184 mesh units, which is 0.18 x 0.18 x 0.18 WORLD CELLS at the renderer's cell of 1024 model units (game/cnc_eyes.cpp MODEL_SCALE = 1/1024; the independent check is a wall straight, authored x[-500,+501], i.e. 1001 units for one cell). A grey steel cube with a lighter recessed panel on each of the four sides. THE CARTRIDGE'S OWN NAME for slots 98 through 105 is ANY_STR_CRATESZ1, all eight the same string, read from the name catalogue, the pointer array at ROM 0x1DE8FC indexed by model-table slot (self-calibrating: it lands GDI_UNIT_ORCAZ1 on slot 53 and ANY_TER_TR01Z1 on slot 113). That array was previously described here as sitting "at ROM 0x1B70F8"; the name blob starts at 0x1B7000 and fourteen named slots point below 0x1B70F8, so the old address was neither the table nor the blob's start. Reproduce with tools/bakery/name_catalogue.py. So the cartridge distinguishes the two crates by MESH, not by name, and there are exactly two crate meshes in the ROM. PLACEMENT, counted over the 100 shipped mission INIs: SCRATE on 8 desert cells in 8 maps and 6 temperate cells in 5 maps. That is a floor and not a total, because the engine also drops wooden crates at run time. Reproduce the render with tools/bakery/render_dl.py --slot 98 --slot 100.

WCRATE.evidence: Code-derived. THE WOODEN GOODIE CRATE, the companion to SCRATE and the commoner of the two in play. Cell-decoration draw table record 36, descriptor RAM 0x8020FF50 = the two s32 {90, -1}: body model id 90, no shadow set. Slot = 90 + 10 = model-table slot 100 (record ROM 0x9ABD8), scene-graph node RAM 0x801B6930, one display list 0x010F3C8 of 8 vertices and 10 triangles, the same ten-of-twelve cube with no bottom face. WHAT SELECTS RECORD 36, read off the registration whose jal is at ROM 0x1959C4: a1 = 0x1C = 28, a2 = RAM 0x801C8628 = "WCRATE", a3 = 0x24 = 36. 28 is OVERLAY_WOOD_CRATE counted from the engine's enum in tiberiandawn/defines.h. SEVEN SLOTS, ONE MESH, and this is the question the slot table poses: model-table records 99, 100, 101, 102, 103, 104 and 105 all carry the IDENTICAL node pointer RAM 0x801B6930. They are not seven crates and not seven crate contents; they are one mesh listed seven times. The reason is the piece-offset arithmetic above: the mode-2 arm adds table[piece].offset to the body id, and that table's offsets run 0..3, so ids 90..93 must all be a crate or a wooden crate on a cell with a non-zero piece index would draw some other model entirely. The run is a guard rail, so ONE mesh is baked and both crate types resolve to one cube each. Ids 94 and 95 (slots 104, 105) are past even that reach: no draw table descriptor anywhere produces them. MEASURED EXTENT 185 x 185 x 184 mesh units = 0.18 cell on a side, the same size as the steel crate. An olive body with dark plank seams and a pale batten up each corner. PLACEMENT, counted over the 100 shipped mission INIs: WCRATE on 12 desert cells in 10 maps and 15 temperate cells in 14 maps, plus every crate MapClass::Place_Random_Crate scatters at run time, which is how a skirmish gets its goodies.
